style: set the scene in one or two plain sentences

candidates.angle: pravritti, the urge to act, is born from rajas
ashamah, restlessness, is the mark of rajas
dvivriddhe, when increased, shows rajas is a growing force

angle_en: Ashamah, restlessness, is the sign of rajas
angle_hi: अशमः, यानी शांति की कमी, रजस का संकेत है

en.intro: Krishna turns from the calm of sattva to the restless force of rajas. Listen for the five signs of this growing energy.
en.notice: Krishna lists the marks of rising rajas: greed, busy activity, fresh undertakings, restlessness and desire.
en.next: Krishna then turns to tamas, the opposite darkness that brings delusion and inertia.
en.meaning: O best of the Bharatas, when rajas grows, greed, activity, the beginning of actions, restlessness, and desire arise.

hi.intro: कृष्ण अब सत्त्व के शांत गुण से रजस की बेचैन ऊर्जा की ओर मुड़ते हैं। इस बढ़ते हुए गुण के पांच संकेत सुनिए।
hi.meaning: हे भरतश्रेष्ठ जब रजोगुण बढ़ता है तो लोभ, प्रवृत्ति, कर्मों का आरम्भ, अशान्ति और स्पृहा ये वृत्तियाँ पैदा होती हैं।
hi.next: कृष्ण फिर तमोगुण की बात करते हैं, जो इसके विपरीत अंधकार, जड़ता और मोह पैदा करता है।

issues: meaning_changed: "अशमः यानी शांति की कमी" (The word 'अशमः' means restlessness or lack of peace. Calling it 'शांति की कमी' (lack of peace) changes the meaning. The Sanskrit 'अ' is a negative prefix, so 'अशमः' means the absence of 'शमः' (tranquility/peacefulness), which is correctly translated as restlessness. 'शांति की कमी' is a weaker and slightly altered meaning.)

wrong_fact: "Notice: Notice the word ashamah, restlessness, lack of peace, which is the sign of rajas, not sattva." (The source verse only lists the signs of rising rajas. It does not mention 'ashamah' (restlessness) as a sign of sattva or contrast it with sattva. The notice introduces an unsupported contrast regarding sattva.)
